title: Find Shortest Route
real_world_story: A warehouse contains aisles and storage positions connected by walkable paths. A worker needs to move from one location to another using the minimum number of moves.

real_world_connection.algorithm_represents: Finding the shortest route between warehouse locations

problem_statement: Given an unweighted warehouse graph with N locations and M connections, find the minimum number of connections required to travel from a starting location S to a destination D. If the destination cannot be reached, return -1.
task: Find the shortest route between two warehouse locations.
input_format: The first line contains two integers N and M. The next M lines contain two integers u and v representing a bidirectional connection between locations u and v. The last line contains two integers S and D representing the starting and destination locations.
output_format: Print the minimum number of connections required to reach D from S. Print -1 if D is unreachable.

examples.explanation: A shortest route is 1 -> 2 -> 4 -> 6, which requires 3 connections.
There is no path connecting location 1 to location 5.

expected_algorithm.name: Graph BFS
expected_algorithm.reason: Breadth-first search explores an unweighted graph level by level and therefore finds the shortest route in terms of connections.

hint: Visit all locations at the current distance before moving farther.
Track the distance of every visited location.
real_world_takeaway: BFS can help warehouse navigation systems find the shortest route between storage locations.
